<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The chunker appears to embed only Description, Comments, and Resolution sections. It likely omits the header line containing the ticket ID and status. This explains why the search fails to locate TKT-1006 despite relevant data existing.

The status and ticket ID live only in metadata JSON, not in the embedded chunk text. Similarity search compares query embeddings against that text, so it cannot match a question asking for the status of TKT-1006 unless the description itself happens to mention the ticket or related terms.

The 0.72 similarity threshold may reject matches entirely. An empty vector store or failed ingestion could also explain the empty results. The chunker stripping the header line is a design bug that prevents ID and status queries from finding relevant data.

Checking AskApiIT tests, reindex endpoints, and startup backfill logic to verify whether existing tickets were properly ingested.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The backend appears to be running despite a 500 error on the health endpoint. I will execute the ask curl request and inspect the vector chunks in the database.

The root cause is likely in the embedding step. TicketChunker extracts text between "Description:" and "Comments:", but the ticket ID and status header sits outside those boundaries. Those headers are therefore not embedded. When the user asks for the status of TKT-1006, the query cannot semantically match the description blocks well enough to exceed the 0.72 similarity threshold. This explains why the system returns no relevant tickets even though the data exists.

Silent ingestion failures are another possibility. TicketService catches errors and logs them without surfacing them. I will check Docker and environment variables, then query the database directly for TKT-1006 chunks and run the ask curl.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

The ticket **is** in Postgres and **is** indexed for RAG. The no-match response comes from **retrieval**, not from missing ticket data or a failed ingest.

## What happened

`AskService` embeds your question, runs vector search, and **short-circuits before the LLM** when every hit is below the similarity threshold:

```35:48:backend/src/main/java/com/ticketmanagement/service/AskService.java
    public AskResult ask(String question) {
        List<float[]> queryVectors = embeddings.embedAll(List.of(question));
        // ...
        List<VectorChunkStore.RetrievedChunk> hits = store.searchSimilar(
                queryVectors.getFirst(),
                retrieval.topK(),
                retrieval.similarityThreshold()
        );
        if (hits.isEmpty()) {
            return new AskResult(NO_MATCH_ANSWER, List.of());
        }
```

Threshold and top-K are configured here:

```43:45:backend/src/main/resources/application.yml
  retrieval:
    top-k: 8
    similarity-threshold: 0.72
```

`JdbcVectorChunkStore` ranks by cosine distance, then **drops** anything with similarity &lt; 0.72.

## Your environment (verified)

| Check | Result |
|--------|--------|
| `GET /api/v1/tickets/TKT-1006` | Ticket exists (OPEN, CRITICAL, etc.) |
| `ticket_vector_chunk` for `TKT-1006` | 1 row: `"User is not able to submit a new ticket"` |
| Ask: *"What is the status of TKT-1006?"* | Best similarity **~0.62** (other ticket), **~0.42** for TKT-1006 → all **&lt; 0.72** → no-match |
| Ask: *"User is not able to submit a new ticket"* | Similarity **1.0** for TKT-1006 → would pass retrieval (generation may be slow on local Ollama) |

So the API is behaving as designed: **semantic search**, not **lookup by ticket id**.

## Why ID/status questions miss

Ingest builds a full document that includes id and status in the **header**:

```51:56:backend/src/main/java/com/ticketmanagement/rag/KnowledgeDocumentBuilder.java
        text.append("Ticket ").append(ticket.getId()).append(": ").append(nullToEmpty(ticket.getTitle())).append('\n');
        text.append("Status: ").append(ticket.getStatus())
                .append(" | Priority: ").append(ticket.getPriority())
```

But `TicketChunker` only embeds **Description**, **Comments**, and **Resolution** — not that header. For TKT-1006 the only embedded text is the description sentence, which is weakly related to *"What is the status of TKT-1006?"* in embedding space.

That matches the spec’s honest no-match path when retrieval is empty or below threshold — it is **not** the same as “ticket doesn’t exist.”

## What works today

Questions that **overlap the indexed text** (description/comments/resolution), e.g. paraphrasing *"User is not able to submit a new ticket"*, can retrieve TKT-1006 and cite it.

## If you want ID/status questions to work

That would be a **product/ingestion change**, for example:

1. **Chunk the header** (ticket id, status, title) into embeddable text, or prepend id/status to each chunk.
2. **Hybrid retrieval**: detect `TKT-\d+` in the question and fetch that ticket’s chunks (or DB row) in addition to vector search.
3. **Lower `similarity-threshold`** — easier but noisier matches.

I can sketch a spec-aligned change (e.g. header chunk + optional ID hybrid) if you want to implement that next.

## Root cause

Vector search only saw **description / comments / resolution**. The assembled document already had **ticket id + status** in the header ([`KnowledgeDocumentBuilder`](backend/src/main/java/com/ticketmanagement/rag/KnowledgeDocumentBuilder.java)), but [`TicketChunker`](backend/src/main/java/com/ticketmanagement/rag/TicketChunker.java) never embedded that block. A question like *“What is the status of TKT-1006?”* did not match the description closely enough to pass **`rag.retrieval.similarity-threshold: 0.72`**.

That matches [`spec/rag-ingestion.md`](spec/rag-ingestion.md) §4 (header in `assembledText` for retrieval) and §6.1 (header as its own region before `Description:`).

## Fix (implemented)

**Embed the header as its own chunk** — ticket id, title, status, priority, assignee, category — before description/comments/resolution.

Changes:

- `TicketChunker.java` — `headerBlocks()` added and wired into the chunk pipeline  
- `TicketChunkerTest.java` — assertion that the header is a searchable chunk  
- `TicketIngestionServiceTest.java` — updated for header + description chunks  

## What you need to do locally

1. **Restart the backend** so it runs the new chunker.

2. **Re-ingest existing tickets** — ingest runs on create/update/comment/status change, not on deploy. Old rows still have only the description embedding. For each ticket you care about, trigger ingest, e.g.:

   ```bash
   curl -s -X PATCH 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/tickets/TKT-1006' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"description":"User is not able to submit a new ticket"}'
   ```

   (Any successful write that schedules ingest is enough.)

3. **Retry ask**:

   ```bash
   curl -s 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ai/ask' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     --data-raw '{"question":"What is the status of TKT-1006?"}'
   ```

   You should get a cited answer with `TKT-1006` in `citedTicketIds` (generation may still take a while on local Ollama).

## What not to rely on

Lowering **`similarity-threshold`** might help some ID questions but adds noisy matches. Skipping the header chunk was the real bug; fixing chunking is the spec-aligned approach.

---

If you want a stronger guarantee for explicit `TKT-####` in the question, a follow-up is **hybrid retrieval** (regex → load that ticket’s chunks plus vector search). Say if you want that added to `AskService`.
